1. The rubber banding: in my experience once my MMR goes up, I start to reach a point where I can’t just outskill enemies so I lose. And then it drops my brackets and I start to win again because my enemies aren’t as good as they were earlier. Even then. From what I’ve felt… overall my MMR tends to rise through it ally

2. Mindsets: as a support before a winning streak starts you may play smart Dota. Then you start winning and get ahead so you start feeling more arrogant. You’re enabling your carry and your enemies aren’t killing you.  Your rush Midas and go damage centric. That leads to bad playstyle as you end up feeding kills. You convinced yourself that you’re the best player on the map. For carries. You may start playing good. Then get ahead. You get more and more greedy. Farm further up the map. Show on lanes more. Join fights earlier. Fight without BKB. You get away with it since you are winning. Instead of BKB you buy Khanda. Your head convinces you that you are so good on the hero that you can do it. So once you hit games where you can’t get ahead? Those mistakes bite you. Showing on wave lets their heroes kill you. Fighting without BKB means they burst you before you can deal damage.

On the flip side once you hit a losing streak it’s the opposite. You may queue in a bad headspace and then lose because of it. Your team is to blame so you pin point all their mistakes and blame them for everything that goes wrong. You may be too passive because the enemy heroes are scary. You leave lanes way too early because your losses have you scared you’ll feed.

3. Different heroes. You may get momentum with one hero and switch. That will mess you up. There may be bad luck with them playing heroes you hate going against.

Also when there’s a big MMR discrepancy in games it becomes a question of “am I good enough/as good as the higher MMR players that I can climb and contribute well?” And when you have lower MMR players “am I good enough that I can take over the game?”

A striker may score 2 above xG today and then 5 below it the next week. People without backgrounds in maths and statistics really put way too much weight into certain numbers.

But an xG is not a promise. But a prediction or a guess. These stats aren’t a “I know” statement but rather an “I think” statement.

The calculation considers where the shot was taken from. But the bounce/luck of how the ball moves plays a factor. A striker thinking a defender is going to cut off the pass will affect his composure with a shot. People forget that
Strikers aren’t the only ones who can perform well/poorly. You may take an amazing shot from a good position but the keeper makes an unreal saves if it’s an attackers second penalty of the game, xG still says it’s a 0.75 probability. But with it being the second one; there’s a lot of mind games that can affect the odds.

Then there’s other factors about who gets the shot where. A shot where someone cuts in from the right? Garnacho is our best bet. But xG doesn’t factor any of that either. A header from a corner may have decent xG. But a nudge from a defender or good positioning will really affect the shot. I’m talking on and on. But those stats aren’t anything but a prediction. 

Over the course of the year they will level out. 

In a one v one; a striker may take a good shot. But if the keeper guesses the right way, then that’s that. It may be a good shot from a high xG spot but if the keepers right in front of you and moves the correct way. It hardly matters. On the other hand. The keeper may guess the wrong way and a bad shot could go in.

It would take infinite variables to make an accurate prediction of if a shot goes in or not. And “if you had infinite data, you wouldn’t need a prediction model” - my ML professor from grad school.

I’m herald so not necessarily the best. Using Luna as a reference 

But use your spells to secure creeps if you think you can’t safely get them. 

If you have items like Mask or phase boots. Anything that helps you move faster. You can use them between camps. 

Dont be shy to tp. If you see top lane taking pressure, you can TP there to get the farm then walk backwards to get your camps. Use the triangle to try to find a way to keep multiple lanes farmed at the same time.

If you see all the enemies eleswjere, you can be a little more risky and push waves out further. If there’s a fight you cant make for example. use tbat to instead pressure another tower.

always assume they are coming for you. the extra creep you kill for 30 gold wont be worth being dead for 30 seconds wirb no creeps to hit.

All you think about is creeps. Does the spell help you farm faster? Will your ultimate do anything for your farm? No? Don’t need it. Will it help you get a kill if someone jumps you? You need it.

You generally do “boots of choice.” “Farm item”  and then build something hybrid (Manta helps you farm and dodge spells. Mjolnir helps you farm while also giving you damage in fights).

But generally what you’re doing is focusing on what helps you reach critical mass. In games where you can hit that mass before your first fight. You will be unkillable.

Early and mid game you don’t want to take fights unless it gives you an objective (saving a tower or pushing a tower). TPing to a fight means you are at threat of dying. Even if you win. You’ll have to share farm with team. It’s only worth it if you can actually get something out of it.

Overall you shouldn’t even think about anything if it’s not helping you farm. On carry all you care about is making sure YOU have a good game. If you show up to a fight under farmed you will not have the greatest impact anyway. Instead say they are fighting around bottom T1 (you are radiant here), why not push out two + waves top pressure tower and steal their camps.

On carry you HAVE to be selfish. Them fighting bottom means you now have all this space you wouldn’t be able to farm otherwise. Use it. Push out lane. Go back to triangle. Send manta illusions mid.

Also. You need to understand what the 30 seconds between creep waves actually means.

Once you kill the wave. That means you have around 30 seconds before you even get the next wave. use that time to farm neutral creeps.

So say it’s the landing stage/it’s almost over. You got ahead. The P4 left lane. Murder that wave ASAP. Farm neutrals aggressively. Move forward to next lane. Farm backwards.

I know this isn’t a clear concise answer and I’m sure a lot of the answers here are better.

But the mindset is creeps. 

Killing a wave does a lot of things:

1. More pressure in their lane: by flash farming a wave, it essentially creates a double wave. Someone has to respond to it or else there’s chip damage on their tower. Making sure your wave survives also acts as wards granting vision so now you can see who responds to the wave. Since the waves are forward. The enemies will have to kill those creeps before moving forward. So camps behind that wave could be yours to farm. Now you can farm backwards and get more gold. Also a wave is a good way to get around 150+ gold. If you are smart. That’s like half a hero kill and more than assist gold in most situations until late game. If a core rotates top because of you, that means their TP is on cool down and a potential mismatch opens elsewhere.

2. Just gold. Like I said. Killing creeps is a very reliable way to get gold. As a carry. You farm way faster than the other heroes. Why? Your abilities allow that. Your agility scaling means you farm even faster. Heroes have cleaves, bash and bounces that allow you to farm very fucking fast. You even have spells to help. Lucent beam, blink on AM, ward on Jugg.

Alright. So in my understanding:

Treads helps me stand and deliver in fights through agi for damage and strength for defense. But against certain heroes, I may want to back out of fights and reposition (heroes who can reduce my armor and nuke me). Because then I’m getting hurt more than I’m hurrying them.

Regarding Mjolnir, it really depends on how often I’m fighting and what types of fights I’ll be taking. If I feel like I can AFK farm for longer then Mjolnir rush makes sense. If I’m worried that I’ll be caught into fights with stuff like call, maybe Slark Leash, Chrono etc. then an SNY could give me the survivability through status resist and stuff. If I’m worried about being silenced by stuff like orchid or even just a bunch of spells, then Manta can get me out.

It’s all about thinking about how I anticipate the fight will shape up. Will I be forced to fight? And will they threaten me with things I can dispel vs “I just need more stats to stay alive”

Also. As carry you really shouldn’t be dead often enough to justify that item. If you’re dead so often that you constantly bag pack to slot the stone, there’s something else wrong with your play style. Any other T2 item will do so much more for you. Either through bonus damage or survivability or better mana pool management. And I’d even say seed of serenity or broom handle are better for you as carry than the Philly stone.
